clinician.trajectory_summary: A 70-year-old man presented with right breast pain, nipple retraction, and skin induration. He had a strong family history of breast cancer. Imaging (mammography and ultrasound) demonstrated a 1.4 cm retroareolar mass with spiculated margins and nipple/skin retraction. A punch biopsy of the nipple-areolar complex showed invasive ductal carcinoma with epidermal involvement, estrogen receptor positive, progesterone receptor positive, and HER2 positive. No separate histologic report specifically describing Paget's disease tumor cell morphology was documented, but the epidermal involvement of tumor cells in the nipple-areolar skin supports the diagnosis of Paget's disease clinically and pathologically.
